/-!
# Normal numbers

A real number $x$ is *normal in base* $b$ if every digit
$d \in \{0,1,\dots,b-1\}$ appears with asymptotic frequency $1/b$
in the base-$b$ expansion of $x$.

A number that is normal in every integer base $b \ge 2$
is called *absolutely normal*.

Despite extensive empirical evidence, it remains unknown whether
classical constants such as $\pi$, $e$, or $\sqrt{2}$ are normal in any base.

*References*:
- [Wikipedia, Normal number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)
- [Wikipedia, Borel normal number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borel_normal_number)

## Main definitions

* `digitSeq`: the sequence of digits in the base-`b` fractional expansion of a real number.
* `IsNormalInBase`: a real number is normal in base `b`.
* `IsAbsolutelyNormal`: a real number is normal in every base `b ≥ 2`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Real Filter

namespace NormalNumber

/-- The `n`-th digit (0-indexed) after the radix point in the base-`b`
expansion of `x`.

Concretely,
`digitSeq b x n = ⌊b^(n+1) * {x}⌋ mod b`,
where `{x}` denotes the fractional part of `x`. -/
noncomputable def digitSeq (b : ℕ) (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ⌊(b : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) * Int.fract x⌋₊ % b

/-- A real number `x` is *normal in base* `b`
if every digit `d < b` appears with asymptotic frequency `1 / b`
in the base-`b` fractional expansion of `x`. -/
noncomputable def IsNormalInBase (b : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ d : ℕ, d < b →
    Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        (((Finset.range n).filter (fun k => digitSeq b x k = d)).card : ℝ) / n)
      atTop
      (nhds (1 / (b : ℝ)))

/-- A real number `x` is *absolutely normal*
if it is normal in every integer base `b ≥ 2`. -/
noncomputable def IsAbsolutelyNormal (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → IsNormalInBase b x

end NormalNumber

findings.description: Lines 63–69 define simple normality, not normality in base b: the only frequency conditions are for individual digits d < b. Normality requires the corresponding conditions for every finite digit block. The module introduction and declaration docstring repeat this incorrect identification. This is a strict mathematical difference: /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves IsNormalInBase 2 (1 / 3 : ℝ), while also proving that its block 00 does not have the required frequency 1/4. Its binary expansion is 0.010101…, so each digit has frequency 1/2 but 00 never occurs.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number, introduction and Definitions, explicitly distinguishes simple normality (each digit has density 1/b) from normality (every length-k string has density b^(-k)); Note 4 gives 0.010101… as a simply normal rational example. Bailey–Crandall, On the Random Character of Fundamental Constant Expansions, §2, Definition 2.1, likewise requires every finite string of k digits to have limiting frequency b^(-k): https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/baicran.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the existing predicate as IsSimplyNormalInBase. Define IsNormalInBase (b : ℕ) (x : ℝ) := ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → IsSimplyNormalInBase (b ^ k) x, using the standard all-positive-powers characterization for b ≥ 2; alternatively quantify directly over every positive-length digit block. Correct the module introduction and declaration docstrings accordingly.

findings.description: FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/NormalityOfPi.lean:40 uses the defective IsNormalInBase predicate, so it asserts only that each decimal digit of π has frequency 1/10. It does not assert the conjectured decimal normality, which also requires every length-k decimal word to have frequency 10^(-k). Fixing the reusable definition is necessary for this declaration to state its intended claim.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi, Irrationality and normality, defines normality by all possible digit sequences of any given length occurring equally often, and records π's normality as unproved. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number, Definitions, gives the precise base-b word-frequency condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the corrected full-normality predicate. With the existing predicate retained under its current name, the required replacement would be ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → NormalNumber.IsNormalInBase (10 ^ k) Real.pi.

findings.description: FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/AlgebraicNormality.lean:50–52 concludes ∃ b, 2 ≤ b ∧ IsNormalInBase b x. With the current library definition this asks whether every irrational algebraic real is simply normal in some base, not normal in some base. Unlike the all-bases conjecture in the same file, this existential quantifier does not supply the frequency conditions in every positive power of the chosen base.
findings.source_evidence: Bailey–Crandall, §1 and §2 Definition 2.1, uses absolute normality for the algebraic-number conjecture and defines normality in an individual base by all finite digit strings: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/baicran.pdf. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number, Properties and examples, discusses algebraic normality and notes that no irrational algebraic number has been proved normal in any base. The file's stated one-base weakening must retain this full meaning of normality, rather than substitute simple normality.
findings.suggested_fix: After separating IsSimplyNormalInBase from full IsNormalInBase, retain the existing existential statement with the corrected full predicate. Equivalently, its conclusion using the current predicate must be ∃ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → NormalNumber.IsNormalInBase (b ^ k) x.

findings.description: The second module reference, at line 36, points to the nonexistent Wikipedia article Borel_normal_number. It does not provide the advertised supporting reference.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borel_normal_number returns HTTP 404 and explicitly says, “Wikipedia does not have an article with this exact name.” The first reference, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number, is valid.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the nonexistent duplicate reference or replace it with an existing mathematical source on Borel normality.

reformulations.difference: Internally this requires simple normality in every integer base b ≥ 2, rather than directly requiring full word-frequency normality in every such base.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These are equivalent. For each fixed b ≥ 2 and every k > 0, b^k ≥ 2, so the definition supplies simple normality in every base b^k. The standard characterization, explicitly stated under Properties in the cited Normal number article, says that this is equivalent to full normality in base b. Conversely, full normality in every base immediately supplies all single-digit conditions. The all-base/all-power quantifier equivalence was proved in scratch.lean; the theorem identifying the power criterion with word-frequency normality was checked mathematically against the source, not formalized in Lean.

reformulations.difference: Its conclusion unfolds to simple normality in every base for every irrational algebraic real, rather than directly spelling out all finite-block frequencies.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The equivalence for NormalNumber.IsAbsolutelyNormal holds pointwise for every real number, so it remains valid under IsIrrationalAlgebraic x and universal quantification over x. Consequently this declaration faithfully states the strong absolute-normality conjecture in Bailey–Crandall §1 despite the incorrect name of the inner base-specific predicate.

reformulations.difference: The existential conclusion uses the current simply-normal predicate, although the docstring refers to full normality in some base.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under this declaration's absolute-normality hypothesis, the stronger intended conclusion also follows: choose base 2, and apply the hypothesis to 2^k for every k > 0 to obtain full base-2 normality by the power characterization. Thus the two existential conclusions are equivalent under the actual hypothesis. A conditional iff to the all-powers formulation was checked in scratch.lean; the connection to arbitrary block frequencies uses the cited mathematical characterization.

submission.summary: Retained the single-digit condition as IsSimplyNormalInBase and defined IsNormalInBase using simple normality in every positive power of the base. Updated the documentation and removed the broken reference; both downstream statements are corrected through the shared definition without editing their files. The required compile check passes without errors or warnings, and both downstream files compile against the updated module with only existing sorry warnings. Regression proofs confirm that 1/3 is simply normal but not normal in base 2, and that absolute normality remains equivalent to its previous formulation.

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Archimedean.Real.Basic
public import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.Pseudo.Defs

/-!
# Normal numbers

For an integer base $b \ge 2$, a real number $x$ is *normal in base* $b$ if,
for every $k \ge 1$, every block of $k$ digits appears with asymptotic frequency
$b^{-k}$ in the base-$b$ expansion of $x$.

Requiring only the single-digit frequencies $1/b$ defines *simple normality*.
Normality in base $b$ is equivalent to simple normality in every base $b^k$
for $k \ge 1$.

A number that is normal in every integer base $b \ge 2$
is called *absolutely normal*.

Despite extensive empirical evidence, it remains unknown whether
classical constants such as $\pi$, $e$, or $\sqrt{2}$ are normal in any base.

*References*:
- [Wikipedia, Normal number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)

## Main definitions

* `digitSeq`: the sequence of digits in the base-`b` fractional expansion of a real number.
* `IsSimplyNormalInBase`: a real number is simply normal in base `b`.
* `IsNormalInBase`: a real number is normal in base `b`.
* `IsAbsolutelyNormal`: a real number is normal in every base `b ≥ 2`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Real Filter

namespace NormalNumber

/-- The `n`-th digit (0-indexed) after the radix point in the base-`b`
expansion of `x`.

Concretely,
`digitSeq b x n = ⌊b^(n+1) * {x}⌋ mod b`,
where `{x}` denotes the fractional part of `x`. -/
noncomputable def digitSeq (b : ℕ) (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ⌊(b : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) * Int.fract x⌋₊ % b

/-- A real number `x` is *simply normal in base* `b`
if every digit `d < b` appears with asymptotic frequency `1 / b`
in the base-`b` fractional expansion of `x`. -/
noncomputable def IsSimplyNormalInBase (b : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ d : ℕ, d < b →
    Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        (((Finset.range n).filter (fun k => digitSeq b x k = d)).card : ℝ) / n)
      atTop
      (nhds (1 / (b : ℝ)))

/-- For `b ≥ 2`, a real number `x` is *normal in base* `b` if every block of `k`
digits appears with asymptotic frequency $b^{-k}$ for every `k ≥ 1`.

We use the equivalent characterization: `x` is simply normal in base `b ^ k`
for every positive integer `k`. -/
noncomputable def IsNormalInBase (b : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → IsSimplyNormalInBase (b ^ k) x

/-- A real number `x` is *absolutely normal*
if it is normal in every integer base `b ≥ 2`. -/
noncomputable def IsAbsolutelyNormal (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → IsNormalInBase b x

end NormalNumber
